public_sources.title: Anytime-Valid Inference Under Outcome Delay: A Design-Based Approach
public_sources.relevance: Primary-source support that outcome value and outcome timing can be coupled and that validity depends on the filtration; used as the timing-selection guard, not as proof of the worker-local redundancy derivations.

public_sources.title: Reproducibility - vLLM
public_sources.relevance: Official documentation: reproducibility is not guaranteed by default; offline deterministic scheduling or online batch invariance is needed, and guarantees are limited to the same hardware and vLLM version.

public_sources.title: Reproducibility - PyTorch 2.13
public_sources.relevance: Official documentation that identical seeds do not guarantee complete reproducibility across releases/platforms and that deterministic algorithms can have performance cost.

public_sources.title: Request Hedging - gRPC
public_sources.relevance: Systems reference for bounded hedged requests, delayed duplicate launch and cancellation; statistical safety in stochastic evaluation is not supplied by this systems contract.

public_sources.title: The Tail at Scale
public_sources.relevance: Primary systems reference showing first-response hedging can sharply reduce tail latency with modest extra request load when replicas are semantically interchangeable.

attempt_identity_semantics.logical_attempt: A statistical attempt is frozen by task/prompt/environment, candidate/incumbent versions, comparison rule, and the complete stochastic identity needed to define one logical output (ideally an explicit random tape/RNG stream rather than only a seed). Physical replicas are identity-preserving only if the execution contract guarantees the same logical output under that frozen identity.
attempt_identity_semantics.same_seed_is_not_sufficient: A seed alone is not treated as proof of identity-preserving replication. Runtime scheduling, hardware, library/version and nondeterministic kernels may change outputs. If deterministic equivalence is not guaranteed, replicas are distinct stochastic attempts for inference.
attempt_identity_semantics.safe_first_completion_case: First-completion hedging is statistically selection-neutral when every physical replica is guaranteed to realize the same frozen logical outcome. Completion order then selects only a physical realization, not a statistical outcome.
attempt_identity_semantics.unsafe_first_completion_case: If replicas are independent or merely potentially different stochastic outputs, fastest/first/best selection can change the logical outcome distribution whenever latency is associated with outcome.

q_preserving_aggregation_result.statement: For m iid Bernoulli(q) stochastic attempts and a permutation-invariant randomized aggregation with a_k = P(output=+ | K=k plus outcomes), requiring P(output=+)=q for every q in [0,1] forces a_k=k/m by uniqueness of the Bernstein-polynomial representation of q. This is distributionally equivalent to selecting one replica uniformly at random independently of values.
q_preserving_aggregation_result.implication: Within this symmetric count-based class, preserving the original single-attempt estimand for all q gives no statistical reason to launch duplicates: preselecting one uniform replica implements the same output law and has the same latency distribution as one attempt. Tail gains from stochastic duplicates therefore require changing the estimand/aggregation, adding a timing-aware inferential model, or establishing identity-preserving replication.
q_preserving_aggregation_result.scope: This is a worker-local derivation for iid Bernoulli attempts and permutation-invariant count-based aggregation required to preserve every q. It is not a universal impossibility theorem for arbitrary structured outcomes, non-iid replicas or conditional timing models.

majority3_safe_aggregate.definition: Freeze three independent stochastic paired attempts; logical sign is their majority. Completion order may be used only to stop/cancel once the predetermined majority is mathematically determined; it may not change which attempts belong to the aggregate.
majority3_safe_aggregate.null_condition: Under conditional global sign-flip symmetry (in particular iid fair signs), the majority sign remains fair even if completion times are sign-associated.
majority3_safe_aggregate.estimand_change: For iid attempt-level candidate-win probability q, logical q_3 = 3q^2 - 2q^3. Thus majority-of-3 evaluates an ensemble/replicated policy, not the original single-attempt policy.
majority3_safe_aggregate.latency_result: If attempt latency is iid and independent of sign with CDF F, majority decision is available by time t with probability F(t)^3 + 0.5*3F(t)^2(1-F(t)) = 1.5F(t)^2 - 0.5F(t)^3, which is strictly below F(t) for 0<F(t)<1. So per-logical-pair majority-of-3 is stochastically slower than one attempt; any whole-audit wall-time gain must come from stronger q_3 causing fewer logical pairs, not faster pair completion.

first_completion_counterexample.exact_toy: Three independent null-fair stochastic attempts have sign +/- with probability 1/2. Let every + finish at time 1 and every - at time 2. Fastest-of-3 is + unless all three are -, hence P(selected +)=7/8. With one-step factor 1.5 for + and 0.5 for -, E[factor]=1.375>1. The e-process null is destroyed even though each underlying attempt is individually fair.
first_completion_counterexample.consequence: Fastest stochastic duplicate selection cannot inherit the single-attempt paired-sign null from marginal fairness alone.

synthetic_redundancy_stress.status: Worker-local synthetic Monte Carlo only; not a deployed model/provider measurement.

model.latency: LogNormal(0,1) multiplied by exp(-0.35) for + and exp(+0.35) for -, plus independent 1% x10 stragglers
model.sequential_wall: sum logical-pair completion times until threshold crossing or pair 50
model.instant_cancel_effective_compute: sum work only until logical decision/cancel; full obligation counts all launched replica durations

policies.identity_replica3: one frozen logical sign with three physical latency replicas; use first completion; valid only if replicas are guaranteed to realize identical logical output
policies.majority3: three independent stochastic signs, predetermined majority, stop only when majority is fixed
policies.unsafe_fastest3: three independent stochastic signs, select fastest completion

synthetic_redundancy_stress.stronger_alternative_note: At attempt-level q=0.70 in the same stress, majority3 achieved commit≈0.9739 and q95 audit wall≈94.94 versus single commit≈0.7387 and q95≈105.20. Thus a safe stochastic aggregate can reduce whole-audit tail for sufficiently strong alternatives, but by changing the estimand and spending substantially more replica work; it does not make each logical pair faster.

identity_preserving_delayed_hedging.definition: Launch one physical replica of the same frozen logical attempt; if it has not completed by a fixed predeclared delay h, launch a second identity-preserving replica; return the first physical completion and cancel the loser. Because both replicas are guaranteed to encode the same logical outcome, even outcome-associated launch/completion timing cannot select a different sign.
identity_preserving_delayed_hedging.synthetic_null_stress: Same latency model as above, two identity-preserving replicas, 400k pairs per delay; baseline delay chosen from the unhedged latency quantiles.
identity_preserving_delayed_hedging.economics_scope: The effective-compute ratios below 1 arise from the deliberately heavy-tailed latency model plus instantaneous cancellation. They are not general. Varying lognormal sigma from 0.2 to 1.6 changed immediate replica3 mean-effective-compute/single from about 2.31x to 0.39x. Always report full launched obligation, effective canceled work and real billing separately.

new_measurement_validity_rules: Make logical attempt identity explicit. A seed is metadata, not proof that two LLM executions are the same stochastic attempt.

Allow first-completion hedging without a timing model only for identity-preserving replicas whose logical outputs are guaranteed equal. Verify the exact determinism contract (model/version/runtime/hardware/random tape/batch-invariance requirements); if that contract is unavailable, classify replicas as distinct stochastic attempts.
For independent stochastic replicas, completion order may determine when a predeclared aggregate is known, but must never determine which replica values define the aggregate.
A safe stochastic aggregate can change the estimand. Report single-attempt q separately from majority/ensemble q and do not describe ensemble power gain as a free evaluation-speedup.

If a purported identity-preserving replica group ever produces divergent logical outputs, fail the determinism gate and do not use fastest-output selection for statistical evidence; treat the run as unresolved/quarantined or fall back to a predeclared canonical attempt.

Log replica_group_id, logical_attempt_id/random-tape or seed, model/runtime/hardware/version fingerprint, aggregation rule fixed before outcomes, launch/finish/cancel times, output hashes and whether cancellation actually stopped compute.
scope_guards: The Bernstein aggregation result is limited to iid Bernoulli attempts, permutation-invariant count-based aggregation and preservation of q for every q.
Majority3 validity uses sign-flip symmetry of the full frozen attempt vector; arbitrary correlated replicas without that symmetry are not covered.

Identity-preserving hedging is only as valid as the deterministic-equivalence contract. Public framework documentation explicitly warns that default/same-seed execution need not be reproducible across schedules, releases or platforms.
Synthetic latency and compute numbers are normalized stress tests, not measurements of any current LLM API, GPU stack, price or cancellation implementation.
The unsafe fastest3 result is an existence/stress demonstration, not a claim about a particular serving system.

frontier.action: Derive and test a determinism-certification protocol for identity-preserving LLM replicas: explicit random tape/seed, batch-invariant scheduling, same runtime/hardware fingerprint, output-hash agreement, and fail-closed handling of any mismatch. Quantify how much p95/p99 latency hedging retains after enforcing deterministic modes and their performance overhead.

For genuinely stochastic replicas where single-attempt estimand must be preserved, investigate richer timing-filtration inference (design-based/IPW or conditional e-process) that can use completion information without fastest-output selection bias; compare against simply freezing one canonical attempt.

Generalize majority-of-3 to m=3/5/7 and randomized symmetric aggregates. Optimize audit-level power versus wall, full/effective compute and estimand distortion; identify regimes where ensemble aggregation reduces total audit wall despite slower logical pairs.

Integrate identity-preserving delayed hedging with the previously certified fixed statistical reveal-order scheduler and hard fail-closed deadlines, including actual preemption/cancel overhead rather than ideal instant cancellation.

exact_next_action: Test whether identity-preserving replication is operationally certifiable for stochastic LLM inference. Build a determinism gate from public vLLM/PyTorch reproducibility contracts, derive fail-closed behavior for mismatch, and quantify tail-latency/compute gains after adding deterministic-mode overhead; in parallel derive whether timing-aware IPW/e-process methods can safely recover first-completion information when replicas are genuinely stochastic.
